newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Gas pipe of Taiwan oil monopoly explodes.
newsitem.headline: Gas pipe of Taiwan oil monopoly explodes.

text.p: An underground gas pipe owned by Taiwan's state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp burst into flames on Saturday, marking the latest in a spate of misfortunes that have hit the company this year.
The pipe, located in the Taipei county of Hsin Chuang, caught fire early on Saturday morning. The flames were extinguished by firefighters within two hours, police officials said by telephone.

Chinese Petroleum, which has suffered more than a dozen accidents in 1996, said in a statement the explosion likely occurred because workers in a nearby construction site accidentally broke the pipe during underground work.
No one was killed or injured in the fire, police said.
Chinese Petroleum said the burst pipe would not affect the company's overall natural gas supply.
"We are repairing the damaged pipe as quickly as we can, but in the meantime gas supply will remain normal," it said.
The accident followed a gas explosion in November at Chinese Petroleum's northern Taoyuan refinery that killed one worker.

Other mishaps -- including fires and oil leaks on land and offshore -- have caused costly shutdowns of the Taoyuan refinery, its crude port and other facilities and cost the oil giant some US$40 million in compensation.
The company's president Chen Kuo-young resigned on November 19 to take responsibility for the accidents.
Its chairman, Chang Tzu-yuan, was ordered by the economics ministry to step down after being indicted on charges unrelated to his duties at Chinese Petroleum.
